Tone Machines reconstructs Applied as the continuation of Jack Gentul's manufacturing work after Hilgen, with the same Kenilworth factory context followed by the Trans-Tek / South Plainfield association and a later Manville move. Treat the corporate chronology as researched history rather than assuming every pedal shared one exact facility.

entity: Applied Big Fuzz / Big Bass family
evidence_summary: The contemporary-facility account explicitly names the Applied Big Fuzz among effects to be built at the Trans-Tek-associated South Plainfield plant; later database naming around Applied Big Bass is not yet sufficient to collapse all Big Fuzz / Big Bass labels into one continuous model identity.

The 1968 historical reconstruction states that a new Trans-Tek plant in South Plainfield housed Trans-Tek and Applied Audio as an associate organization and that the facility would build amplifiers and effects pedals. This is facility evidence, not proof that Trans-Tek itself manufactured every Applied-branded unit.

Bob Seidman's LIMMCO is documented as a wholesale and distribution hub connecting Applied, Nomad, Kimberly, UMI, Guild, Goya and other East Coast effects brands. LIMMCO should not be treated as the physical builder except for the earliest Kimberly v1 state explicitly attributed to LIMMCO.
